title: Board of Trustees Regular Meeting-1st
overview: Based on the published agenda, the Board of Trustees of the Village of Port Chester was scheduled to hold a regular meeting to address zoning amendments for two development projects, approve budget transfers, and discuss procedural matters related to street closures and special event permits. The meeting was set to include public hearings on extending building permit timelines for the 155-157 Irving Avenue and 157 Westchester Avenue projects.

Award Presentation - Recognition of Pirates 12U
Department of Code Enforcement Presentation by Acting Director Michael J. Panella
Public hearing on local law amending Chapter 345 Zoning to provide 155-157 Irving Avenue project additional time to secure building permit; Resolution 0.5 adopting Local Law No. I-XX of 2026
Public hearing on local law amending Chapter 345 Zoning to provide 157 Westchester Avenue project additional time to secure building permit; Resolution 0.75 adopting Local Law No. I-XXI of 2026
Discussion on setting defined time frame for street closure requests, police escort requests, and Village property use permits
Approval of September 2, 8, 23 and 30, 2026 minutes
Report of the Village Manager
Resolution - Budget Transfer Fiscal Year 2026-27 General Fund Fire Department in amount of $4,950
Resolution - Free parking for 2026 Holiday Season
Correspondence from Vincent A. Lyons, Chairman, American Legion Port Chester Post 93 regarding Veterans Day
Public Comments and Board Comments
Proposed Executive/Closed Session

discussions.item: 155-157 Irving Avenue Project Zoning Amendment and Building Permit Timeline Extension
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to conduct a public hearing on a proposed local law amendment to Chapter 345 Zoning that would provide the 155-157 Irving Avenue project additional time to secure a building permit under its existing Site Plan Approval from November 27, 2023. The Board was expected to consider Resolution 0.5, which would find the action to be a Qualified Action exempt from SEQRA review and adopt Local Law No. I-XX of 2026.

discussions.item: 157 Westchester Avenue Project Zoning Amendment and Building Permit Timeline Extension
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to conduct a public hearing on a proposed local law amendment to Chapter 345 Zoning that would provide the 157 Westchester Avenue project additional time to secure a building permit under its existing Site Plan Approval from November 27, 2023. The Board was expected to consider Resolution 0.75, which would find the action to be a Qualified Action exempt from SEQRA review and adopt Local Law No. I-XXI of 2026.

discussions.item: Defined Time Frame for Street Closures and Special Event Permits
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to discuss setting a defined time frame for requests related to street closures, police escorts, and use of Village property. This discussion item was carried over from the October 5 meeting and was requested by the Board of Trustees.

discussions.item: Department of Code Enforcement Presentation
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to receive a presentation from Acting Director of Code Enforcement Michael J. Panella regarding the Department of Code Enforcement's activities and operations.

discussions.item: Budget Transfer - Fire Department
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to consider a budget transfer resolution for the Fiscal Year 2026-27 General Fund Fire Department in the amount of $4,950.

discussions.item: Free Parking for 2026 Holiday Season
discussions.body: The Board was scheduled to consider a resolution providing free parking for the Village during the 2026 Holiday Season.

publicComment: Public comment was indicated on the agenda at two points: once during the dedicated Public Comments section (VII) and again during Public Comments and Board Comments (XI).

The meeting was also set to consider a resolution establishing a public hearing on graduated parking violation fines.

discussions.body: The board was scheduled to discuss safety concerns related to e-bikes and scooters operating within Port Chester. The discussion was expected to address regulatory or public awareness measures to promote safe use of these devices in residential and commercial areas.

discussions.item: Update on IMA with the Town of Rye regarding outstanding parking ticket collection
discussions.body: The board was set to receive an update on the intermunicipal agreement with the Town of Rye concerning the collection of outstanding parking tickets. This item was carried forward from the October 5 meeting and was expected to address coordination efforts and collection status.

discussions.item: Setting term limits for the Mayor and Board of Trustees
discussions.body: The board was scheduled to discuss the establishment of term limits for the Mayor and Trustees. This governance matter was expected to consider policy changes regarding tenure for elected officials.

discussions.item: Revise Board Agenda Processes and Board Policies & Procedures
discussions.body: The board was set to review and discuss potential revisions to its agenda processes and overall policies and procedures. This item was expected to address operational and governance framework improvements.

discussions.item: Discussion on murals
discussions.body: The board was scheduled to discuss matters related to murals within the village. This discussion was expected to address policies, locations, or approvals for public or private mural projects.

discussions.item: Discussion on criteria for providing site plan extension approvals
discussions.body: The board was set to discuss the establishment or revision of criteria for approving site plan extensions. This planning and zoning matter was expected to clarify standards for developers seeking project timeline extensions.

discussions.item: Discussion on Day Care centers
discussions.body: The board was scheduled to discuss issues or policies related to day care centers operating in Port Chester. This discussion was expected to address licensing, operations, or regulatory matters affecting childcare facilities.

discussions.item: RFP 2026-07 - Professional Consulting Services for Residential Parking, Traffic Circulation, and Public Safety Study
discussions.body: The board was set to consider a Request for Proposals for professional consulting services to conduct a comprehensive study on residential parking, traffic circulation, and public safety. This procurement was expected to lead to a selection of consultants to analyze transportation and safety issues in the village.

discussions.item: Discussion on choosing who can chair a committee
discussions.body: The board was scheduled to discuss procedures and criteria for selecting committee chairs. This governance matter was expected to address leadership structure and appointment processes for village committees.

title: Planning Commission Meeting
overview: Based on the published agenda, the Port Chester Planning Commission was scheduled to hold a regular meeting to review and conduct public hearings on four applications involving property modifications and changes of use across the village. The agenda included consideration of a church building extension, a commercial tenant space conversion, an outdoor dining area addition, and a Costco expansion project.

agenda.item: Approval of Minutes from September 28, 2026
Public Hearing - Case #2024-0255: 35 Traverse Avenue - Modification of existing building with new two story rear extension for Spanish United Pentecostal Church
Public Hearing - Case #2026-0275: 21 Grace Church Street - Site Plan approval and Special Exception Use Approval for change of use for Coffee Holding Company Inc.
Public Hearing - Case #2026-0274: 179 Rectory Street - Creation of outdoor dining area adjacent to existing restaurant for The Sonora Group
Public Hearing - Case #2026-0276: 1 Westchester Avenue - Request to Adjourn for Costco Wholesale Corporation expansion and exterior stairs addition

discussions.item: Case #2024-0255 - 35 Traverse Avenue
discussions.body: The Commission was scheduled to conduct a public hearing on an application submitted by Ana Soto Fedigan on behalf of Spanish United Pentecostal Church for modification of the existing building at 35 Traverse Avenue with the addition of a new two-story rear extension. The property is located in Section 142.39, Block 1, Lot 38.

discussions.item: Case #2026-0275 - 21 Grace Church Street
discussions.body: The Commission was set to hold a public hearing on an application submitted by Aldo Vitagliano Esq. on behalf of Coffee Holding Company Inc. for Site Plan approval and Special Exception Use Approval regarding a change of use in one tenant space at 21 Grace Church Street. The application involves conversion of a space that currently houses coffee manufacturing with a marble and stone processing subtenant.

discussions.item: Case #2026-0274 - 179 Rectory Street
discussions.body: The Commission was scheduled to conduct a public hearing on an application submitted by The Sonora Group and Rafael Palomino for the creation of an outdoor dining area adjacent to an existing restaurant at 179 Rectory Street. The property is located in Section 136.71, Block 1, Lot 50.

discussions.item: Case #2026-0276 - 1 Westchester Avenue
discussions.body: The Commission was set to consider a request to adjourn on an application submitted by Nick Tose, Director of Real Estate for Costco Wholesale Corporation, for the expansion of the southeast corner of the building and addition of exterior stairs at 1 Westchester Avenue. The property is located in Section 142.31, Block 1, Lot 1.

The meeting was also set to include a presentation from the Police Chief and consideration of public parking accommodation requests.

discussions.body: The Board was set to consider correspondence from Jon Haseltine on behalf of Meals on Main Street requesting the Village designate 3-4 curbside parking spaces directly adjacent to their location at 509-511 North Main Street.

discussions.item: Case #2026-0262: D&B Company Shipping Containers Interpretation

title: Industrial Development Agency (IDA) Regular Meeting
overview: The Port Chester Industrial Development Agency approved the Initial Project Resolution for AMS Acquisitions' Westchester Crossing Senior Living Pad project and authorized a budget amendment, but rejected a staff contract renewal motion. The board also voted to reconsider a fee amendment to the Assignment Policy and approved October invoices before entering executive session.

agenda.item: IDA Roll Call
Approval of Minutes from September 9, 2026

AMS Acquisitions application review for the Westchester Crossing Senior Living Pad, including AKRF memo on site plan amendments, Senior Living Pad assignment request from Boston Post Road Owner LLC, application, and Initial Project Resolution
Staff Contract renewals
Adjust fees for Project Assignments under PCIDA Assignment Policy
AD Report including updates on proposed 227 Westchester Ave and 208-216 King Street projects and prospects for a downtown Welcome Center

discussions.item: Motion to Open Meeting
discussions.body: The board voted to open the meeting. Motion passed 5-0, moved by James Taylor and seconded by Sylvia Dundon. Board members voting yes: Richard O'Connell, James Taylor, Sylvia Dundon, Daniel Brakewood, and Francis Ferrara.

discussions.item: Approval of Minutes from September 9, 2026
discussions.body: Motion to approve the September 9, 2026 minutes passed without recorded vote count or dissent.

discussions.item: AMS Acquisitions Initial Project Resolution for Westchester Crossing Senior Living Pad
discussions.body: The board approved the Initial Project Resolution for AMS Acquisitions' Westchester Crossing Senior Living Pad project, which included review of the AKRF memo on site plan amendments presented by Greg Cutler, the Senior Living Pad assignment request from Boston Post Road Owner LLC, and the application. Motion passed without recorded vote count or dissent.

discussions.item: Staff Contract renewals
discussions.body: Motion to approve staff contracts failed. The vote record does not indicate the vote count or which board members voted for or against the motion.

discussions.item: Adjust fees for Project Assignments under PCIDA Assignment Policy
discussions.body: Motion to reconsider fee amendment to the Assignment Policy passed without recorded vote count or dissent.

discussions.item: Approval of October 2026 Monthly Invoices
discussions.body: Motion to approve monthly invoices for October 2026 passed without recorded vote count or dissent.

discussions.item: Budget Amendment
discussions.body: Motion to approve budget amendment passed without recorded vote count or dissent.

discussions.item: Executive Session
discussions.body: Motion to enter into executive session passed 4-0, moved by Sylvia Dundon and seconded by Daniel Brakewood. Board members voting yes: James Taylor, Sylvia Dundon, Daniel Brakewood, and Francis Ferrara.

actionItems: Westchester Crossing Senior Living Pad project by AMS Acquisitions advanced with Initial Project Resolution approved

title: Local Development Corporation (LDC) Regular Meeting
overview: Based on the published agenda, the Port Chester Local Development Corporation was scheduled to consider establishment of a non-profit grant program, review staff recommendations for grant awards, and deliberate on a request for proposals for consulting services focused on commercial displacement mitigation strategies. The meeting was also set to address routine financial and administrative matters including treasurer reports and website updates.

agenda.item: Approval of Minutes from August 19, 2026
Resolution Establishing a Non-Profit Grant Program and Form a Grant Agreement
Staff Recommendation for Non-Profit Grant Award (Chris Steers)
Final Draft of RFP for Consulting Services to Develop Commercial Displacement Mitigation Strategies
Update on LDC Website (Rosalind Cimino)
Treasurer's Report (Tony Siligato)

discussions.item: Resolution Establishing a Non-Profit Grant Program and Form a Grant Agreement
discussions.body: The LDC was scheduled to consider a resolution to establish a non-profit grant program and form associated grant agreements. This item was set to outline the framework and procedures for distributing grants to eligible non-profit organizations in the Port Chester area.

discussions.item: Staff Recommendation for Non-Profit Grant Award
discussions.body: Staff member Chris Steers was scheduled to present recommendations for non-profit grant awards to the board. The presentation was expected to provide details on recommended recipients and rationale for the proposed awards.

discussions.item: Final Draft of RFP for Consulting Services to Develop Commercial Displacement Mitigation Strategies
discussions.body: The LDC was set to review the final draft of a request for proposals for consulting services aimed at developing strategies to mitigate commercial displacement. This item was scheduled to address how the corporation plans to support local businesses and communities facing potential displacement pressures.

discussions.item: Update on LDC Website
discussions.body: Rosalind Cimino was scheduled to provide an update on the development and status of the LDC website. The update was expected to inform the board on progress related to the organization's online presence and information accessibility.

discussions.item: Treasurer's Report
discussions.body: Tony Siligato was scheduled to present the treasurer's report, which was set to include approval of invoices and a budget amendment for auditor expenses. The report was expected to provide financial updates and require board action on expenditure matters.

Expected to vote on resolution establishing a non-profit grant program and grant agreement form
Scheduled to consider staff recommendations for non-profit grant awards

Expected to approve invoices and budget amendment for auditor expense
